_comment: Mutation testing for the optional-feature flag resolver. featureFlags.js is a small file that decides something consequential: whether a stored WorkerConfig override wins over an env-var default, per flag. A test that merely executed those lines would still pass if the precedence were inverted, so line coverage says nothing here — mutation does. Scoped to src/featureFlags.js and its OWN unit test (vitest.stryker.features.config.js), which is fully mocked and reads no real filesystem, so it runs clean inside Stryker's app/api-only sandbox. Run: cd app/api && npm run test:mutation:features. MUTATION FLOOR: `break` is set a few points under the measured score and is a RATCHET — it only goes up. Enforced by the weekly .github/workflows/js-mutation.yml, never on a PR. Raise it when the score rises; never lower it to make a red run green — a drop means a test stopped discriminating. Measured 100.0% when the floor was set to 98.

mutationExclusions.src/ontology/vocabulary.js: Core ontology tooling (developer and CI check, never loaded by the server). Not yet measured: Stryker's vitest runner does not activate mutants on the Windows workstation this was written on, so any score quoted here would be fiction. The IRI constants and type maps are exercised by every ontology test, and a wrong SQL-to-XSD or ingest-to-SQL entry fails src/ontology/checks/integrity.test.js / implementation.test.js and the real-repository guard. Measure it on Linux and move it into a scope's mutate list.

Parsing and flattening are pinned by src/ontology/model.test.js against a small clean fixture with exact expected structures (union domains in order, value-set precedence, cycle-safe subclass walk). Measure it on Linux and move it into a scope's mutate list.

The decisions in this file are pinned by src/ingest/reconcileStale.test.js with discriminating inputs -- the request parser is asserted against every rejection it can make (unknown entity, each of the five entities that carry no system scope, a non-integer or non-positive systemId, an unparseable or future timestamp), and the SQL builder is asserted on the soft-delete vs hard-delete split, the deletedAt IS NULL guard, the scope filter and the parameter ordering. The route wiring is covered in src/routes/ingest.coverage.test.js and the crawler side of the protocol (reconcile only after a completed run that fed the system) in test/unit/CSVCrawlerPhases.Tests.ps1 and, for the SQL Server crawler, tools/crawlers/mssql/Test-SqlCrawler.ps1. mutationExclusions.src/ingest/managerLinks.js: Not yet measured, for the same reason as the ingest files above: Stryker's vitest runner does not activate mutants on the Windows workstation this was written on, so any score quoted here would be fiction. The file is one SQL constant plus four decisions, and each is pinned by a discriminating test in src/ingest/managerLinks.test.js: the table gate and the missing-system gate are asserted by `query` NOT being called (so removing either fails, which a call-count-free test would not catch), systemId 0 is asserted to still run (so the guard cannot be rewritten as a truthiness check), zero counts are asserted to return null and non-zero to return the pair, and the warning text is asserted for each half separately and for both together. What the SQL actually selects — that a resolved link survives, an unresolvable one and a self-reference are cleared and counted apart, another system's rows are untouched, and a soft-deleted manager still counts as existing — is only meaningful against PostgreSQL and is verified there by contract-tests/managerLinks.contract.test.js. Measure it on Linux and move it into a scope's mutate list.
mutationExclusions.src/ingest/initialLoad.js: Initial-load history flag (migration 073): one SELECT of Systems.lastSyncDateTime and one SET LOCAL. What it decides only means something against PostgreSQL — that the history INSERT trigger skips rows while the transaction-local setting is on, that deletes and later syncs are still recorded, and that the setting does not outlive its transaction — which contract-tests/historyInitialLoad.contract.test.js verifies through the real ingest engine. Its three branches (no system, synced system, unsynced system) are each pinned by src/ingest/initialLoad.test.js.
